title: Comfort without surrender
lines: Imagine an automated order offering comfort, safety and varied experiences, if you hand it governance.
This book takes that offer seriously, answering with twenty-one debatable clauses of a new social contract.
Its fear is not scarcity, but a leadership that controls automated infrastructure and cannot be replaced.

emotionalPlan.arc: Curiosity at a tempting offer, sharpening into concern about irreplaceable control.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book, its central offer and why it deserves attention within the first thirty seconds.
voiceDirections: Open warmly, as if presenting a genuine invitation.
Firm and clear; land on twenty-one clauses.
Lower and more serious; stress cannot be replaced.

title: Delegate, never surrender
lines: Administration may be delegated to automated systems, but collective goals must stay under legitimate control.
A right to leave a provider counts only if identity, records and services move too.
An appeal needs reasons, corrected facts, independent review and a real remedy.
Those who set goals, run infrastructure and oversee rights must remain separate powers.

title: Clauses under stress
lines: Later clauses protect attention, privacy, ecological budgets, reproductive freedom and room for new generations.
The final chapters ask who pays, who enforces, and why powerful actors would comply.
Its test is clear: abundance is legitimate when it reduces dependency, not when it makes dependency comfortable.
Begin with the Introduction, where the book sets out the political offer of an automated order.
